catalogTitle: יארצייט: יארצייט של ר' שרגא פייוול מענדלאוויץ זצ”ל (ג' אלול)

oneLiner.en: On the yahrtzeit of Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, the Mashgiach describes him as an eved Hashem whose whole life was a Shabbos niggun of shleimus and harmony, a song that still sings in the yeshiva.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the end of the Torah: Moshe is called both 'ish ha'Elokim' and 'eved Hashem', and Yehoshua, who wrote the last pesukim, could describe him only from his own level, as eved Hashem. Like a blade of grass that also benefits from the sun, the Mashgiach will describe Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz as an eved Hashem: a builder of Torah in America who sat in the last bench and refused titles. His deepest teacher was his own neshamah, a neshamah of Shabbos, which is shleimus, and of shirah, which is harmony, like seven notes making one melody. The Mashgiach brings the 'seventh' in creation, Eretz Yisrael as a land of song, and stories of a torn leaf whose song was interrupted. Every life is a niggun; his was a Shabbos niggun, seen in his love of creation's beauty, the flowers he planted, the harmony he made between groups, the best talmidim he gave away, and his kabbalos. His niggun still sings.

en: Yehoshua could describe Moshe only as 'eved Hashem', from his own level; likewise the Mashgiach describes Reb Shraga Feivel as an eved Hashem.
Reb Shraga Feivel built Torah in America yet wanted no honor or title, preferring to remain a plain Jew.
His main teacher was his own neshamah, a neshamah of Shabbos and of shirah: Shabbos is shleimus, and shirah is harmony.
Every part of creation sings shirah to Hashem, and every person's life is a niggun; his life was one long Shabbos niggun.
As an eved Hashem he sent his best talmidim to build other yeshivos, and his niggun still sings in the yeshiva.

candidateTopics: chinuch of each bochur according to his way

title.en: Moshe: ish ha'Elokim and eved Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the last parsha of the Torah, where Moshe is called 'ish ha'Elokim', and explains that Yehoshua, who wrote the last pesukim, could describe him only as 'eved Hashem'. Comparing himself to a blade of grass that also benefits from the sun, he says he too will try to describe Reb Shraga Feivel.

title.en: A builder of Torah who sat in the last bench

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Reb Shraga Feivel as an eved Hashem: he planted Torah in America, yet sought no honor, sat in the last bench at the dedication of the new building he had organized, and taught his talmidim Tanya and Shaarei Teshuvah. He did not take a title and preferred to remain a plain Jew.

title.en: A neshamah of Shabbos and of shirah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Reb Shraga Feivel's main rebbe was his own neshamah, a Shabbos neshamah: on Erev Shabbos he became a different person. Shabbos is shleimus, and shirah is harmony, like seven notes; he brings the 'seventh' in creation and Eretz Yisrael as a land of song, and concludes that Reb Shraga Feivel was not limited to one area but was a neshamah of shleimus.

title.en: The leaf that sings

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how in camp Reb Shraga Feivel stopped a talmid who tore off a leaf, since he had interrupted its shirah, and how in Monsey he saw one leaf moving among still ones as the chazan. He adds that Reb Shraga Feivel would repeat that every person's life is a niggun sung to Hashem.

title.en: Beauty of creation and harmony between groups

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Reb Shraga Feivel taught bochurim to develop a sense for the beauty of creation in order to thank Hashem, bringing David Hamelech and the Rambam. In Monsey he planted flowers among the first things, and in the yeshiva he made a harmony between Hungarian Jews, Litvish roshei yeshiva and chassidus.

title.en: Giving away his best talmidim

summary.en: The Mashgiach relates that Reb Shraga Feivel sent his best talmidim to found other yeshivos, and he tells the bochurim to remember, when they are in business, what it means to give one's best people to a competitor. He did this because he was an eved Hashem.

title.en: A path for each bochur; the niggun still sings

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Reb Shraga Feivel had no single method but a separate path for each bochur, and tells of kabbalos found after his passing: to find a new idea every day to improve the yeshiva and to love every bochur. He concludes that his spirit remains in the yeshiva and his niggun is still sung.

catalogTitle: הכנסת כלה: א מצוה באזונדער מסוגל אויף ביאת המשיח (ביאור ענין יחוד קוב"ה ושכינתיה' עניניא דיומא - ערד ציטערניש בהייטי)

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that hachnasas kallah stands out among the mitzvos as a source of rescue and of bringing the geulah, because the aim of every mitzvah is the union of Hashem, the Chassan, with Klal Yisrael, the Kallah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the teaching of Rabbi Dovid of Lelov that hachnasas kallah, placed in the list of birchos hashachar between visiting the sick and what comes after, saves a person from what follows it, and says one should give for it knowing it is a great rescue. He turns to the unsettled times and the earthquake in Haiti, citing the passuk in Tehillim that Hashem looks at the earth and it trembles, and tells how the Chofetz Chaim gathered his town in Radin to speak about a flood on the Mississippi. He explains the reason from Rashi in Parshas Va'eira: Hashem brings punishment on the nations so that the Jews take mussar, and he calls for strengthening in every area. Then he explains 'leshem yichud': every mitzvah aims at uniting the Chassan and the Kallah, so hachnasas kallah itself arouses Heaven most, and he closes with a brachah for the geulah.

en: Following Rabbi Dovid of Lelov, hachnasas kallah stands between visiting the sick and what follows it because it rescues a person from what comes after.
A disaster among the nations, like the earthquake in Haiti, is meant for the Jews, as Rashi says that Hashem punishes the nations so that the Jews will fear and take mussar.
The Mashgiach says Jews must take this to heart and strengthen themselves in every area, including the chinuch of children and tznius in dress.
Every mitzvah is said 'leshem yichud', for the union of Hashem, the Chassan of Shir Hashirim, with Klal Yisrael, His Kallah, who are now apart in galus.
Since the aim of every mitzvah is a kind of hachnasas kallah, the actual mitzvah of hachnasas kallah arouses Heaven more than any other.

candidateTopics: Hashem and Klal Yisrael as chassan and kallah

title.en: Hachnasas kallah rescues from what follows

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the great nachas in Heaven from helping Jews marry off their children, and brings Rabbi Dovid of Lelov's teaching that hachnasas kallah, placed in birchos hashachar between visiting the sick and what follows, saves from what comes after. He says that had he known this, he would have given far more, and that one should give knowing it is a great rescue from harsh decrees.

title.en: The Haiti earthquake and the Chofetz Chaim

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the unsettled times and the earthquake in Haiti, brings the passuk in Tehillim that Hashem looks at the earth and it trembles, and asks what it has to do with Jews. He tells how the Chofetz Chaim gathered the whole town of Radin for a drasha about a flood on the Mississippi, so that people should not ignore it.

title.en: Rashi in Va'eira: punishment of nations is for the Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the earthquake came in the week of Parshas Va'eira, where Rashi brings the passuk in Tzefaniah that Hashem destroys nations so that the Jews will fear and take mussar. He explains that the disaster is a message to Jews everywhere, that great plans for geulah are being prepared in Heaven, and that Jews must strengthen themselves in every area.

title.en: Leshem yichud: the Chassan and the Kallah

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why hachnasas kallah, of all mitzvos, is the one placed as the interruption. He explains 'leshem yichud' said before every mitzvah: Hashem and Klal Yisrael are Chassan and Kallah as in Shir Hashirim, separated in galus, and every mitzvah aims at their union in the geulah.

title.en: Collectors during davening; the women's resolution

summary.en: The Mashgiach addresses complaints about collectors for hachnasas kallah going around during davening and says he thanks such a person, because he reminds him that his davening is meant to be hachnasas kallah. He praises the women's resolution to work for hachnasas kallah, the mitzvah that arouses Heaven most, and closes with a brachah for the geulah.

catalogTitle: The Beginning of our Nuptials with Hashem

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains Pesach as the beginning and the opening of the bond between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, with the matzah as the key that opens a higher world for every Jew.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the idea that Pesach is the first stage of the nuptials between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, lesser than Shavuos and Sukkos, yet its prohibition of chametz carries kares, because eating matzah binds a Jew to Hashem just as strongly. Pesach is the reishis that holds everything, a time of renewal: the joy in Heaven in Nisan is mirrored in the reawakening of nature and in Shir Hashirim, and it is a time of techiyas hameisim and of becoming a new person. He then contrasts bread, which contains the ten utterances of creation and equals three times the Name of Hashem (78), with matzah, three times the full spelling of the Name (135), drawn from the world of 'Mah' that one can only ask about. Matzah is the key to rebirth and to opening up; Hashem knocks and asks Klal Yisrael to open for Him. He closes with tefillah for the geulah, seeing and being seen on Yom Tov, and wanting to be redeemed.

en: Pesach is the beginning of the bond between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, lesser than the later Yamim Tovim, yet its chametz prohibition carries kares because eating matzah binds a Jew to Hashem.
Pesach is the reishis that contains everything and a time of renewal, mirrored in the reawakening of nature in Nisan.
Bread contains the ten utterances of creation and therefore satisfies every kind of person, but its holiness is received only when one eats as a Jew should.
Matzah, equal to three times the full spelling of Hashem's Name, comes from a higher source than bread and is the key that opens a world beyond grasp.
On Pesach every Jew goes through a rebirth, and Hashem knocks on the door and asks Klal Yisrael to open up to Him.
Each Yom Tov has its gift; the gift of Pesach is geulah, and only one who wants it receives it.

candidateTopics: Pesach as the beginning of the bond with Hashem

title.en: Pesach as the first stage, and the kares of chametz

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Pesach as the beginning of the nuptials with Hashem, lesser than Shavuos and Sukkos (full Hallel, chametz still unfit), and asks why its prohibition alone carries kares. He answers that kares cuts the bond, while eating matzah creates hiskashrus, binding a Jew to Hashem.

title.en: Reishis, renewal and the joy of Nisan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains Pesach as the reishis that contains everything and as the renewal of the bond with Hashem. The joy in Heaven, shown in the tzeruf of Nisan from 'Yismechu hashamayim', comes down to earth: a new nation is born, nature wakes up in spring, and Shlomo HaMelech put this theme into Shir Hashirim.

title.en: Techiyas hameisim and becoming new

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the tradition that techiyas hameisim will be on Pesach and connects it to the dew of life, for which we begin praying on Pesach. He says it is a time for every Jew to make a reckoning and become a new person, and shows the flavor of newness in the custom of new clothes, dishes and painting for Pesach.

title.en: Bread holds the ten utterances

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why Hamotzi has ten words: bread contains the ten utterances of creation, just as man, created last, contains all traits, though each person has a dominant one. Therefore people need variety in food but never tire of bread; yet one who eats like Esav, without a bracha, receives klipah instead of that holiness.

title.en: The Malbim: how a Jew eats

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Malbim, after a debate with maskilim, said that they may know much, but he knows how to eat, and listed the many steps a Jew takes before he may eat. He adds that bread holds a threefold holiness, three times the Name of Hashem, equal to lechem (78), which gives life to the soul.

title.en: Matzah: three times Mah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that matzah comes from a higher root than bread: Adam equals 45, the full spelling of the Name, called 'Mah', the world beyond grasp from which Yetzias Mitzrayim came. That is why the Seder opens with questions, and matzah, three times 45 (135), is the key to that world, eaten three times at the Seder.

title.en: The key of birth and opening

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains Yetzias Mitzrayim as a birth, a nation taken from within a nation, and brings the Gemara that Hashem keeps the keys of birth and techiyas hameisim himself: on Pesach every Jew is reborn through the matzah. He connects this to 'peter rechem', to Targum's 'patira' for matzah, to the opening of the aron with Brich Shmei, and to 'Pischi li' in Shir Hashirim.

title.en: Tal, the matzah capsule and the open door

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the tal (39, the first letters of the Name in full spelling) comes down to the final hei, Klal Yisrael, and that is the matzah. He brings the Ba'al HaTanya that the flour and water are only a capsule holding the same light as the matzah eaten in Mitzrayim, and ends with opening the door for Eliyahu HaNavi, since all of Pesach is an opening.

title.en: Tefillah for the King, re'iyah, and wanting geulah

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls the day Rosh Hashanah for kings, when appointments are made in Heaven, and says one should daven that Hashem alone be King, with Moshiach as His chariot. He speaks of seeing Hashem and being seen on Yom Tov with completeness, and closes that the gift of Pesach is geulah, which only one who wants to be freed from the yetzer hara receives.

catalogTitle: סעודת הודאה: סעודת הודאה - ר"ח ניסן (ור' מרדכי פינקלמאן)

oneLiner.en: At a seudas hodaah on the eve of Rosh Chodesh Nissan, the Mashgiach explains that a Jew must praise Hashem with his life and with every extra year he is given, and that the days of the nesiim are days of chinuch, of starting anew.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the passuk 'I will praise Hashem with my life' and brings the Kedushas Levi: everything was created for Hashem's honor, even the rasha, whose 'song' is his downfall, while the tzaddik praises Hashem with his life. He tells of two times the Gerrer Rebbe, for whom every minute counted, was 'defeated': by a man struggling twenty years with a sick daughter, and by a blind chassid who did not want 'gifted years' without learning. From this he reads 'with my extra being' as praising Hashem with the extra years. After a story of a chassid of the Ba'al HaTanya, he says every Jew must contemplate his tafkid. The twelve days of the nesiim, whose korbanos defeat the nesiim of Yishmael, are days of chinuch, of starting anew; he closes with a brachah for the Beis HaMikdash.

en: According to the Mashgiach, a Jew must praise the Ribono shel Olam with his life itself, as the passuk says 'I will praise Hashem with my life'.
Everything, even the rasha, was created for Hashem's honor; the rasha brings it out through his downfall, the tzaddik through his life.
The extra years a person is given are meant to be used to sing to Hashem, not merely to be lived through.
Every Jew came into the world for a particular tafkid, and should contemplate what it is.
The twelve days of the nesiim are days of chinuch, in which one leaves the old behind and begins anew.

title.en: Opening

summary.en: Opening.

title.en: Praising Hashem with one's life and extra years

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Kedushas Levi on 'I will praise Hashem with my life': the rasha glorifies Hashem through his downfall, the tzaddik with his life. He tells of the two times the Gerrer Rebbe was 'defeated', the second by a blind chassid who did not want 'gifted years', and reads 'with my extra being' as singing to Hashem with the extra years.

title.en: Every Jew's tafkid; the days of the nesiim

summary.en: After a story of a chassid who asked the Ba'al HaTanya for years he could accomplish something with, the Mashgiach says each person must contemplate his tafkid. He explains that the twelve days of the nesiim, beginning that night, defeat the nesiim of Yishmael and are days of chinuch for renewing oneself, and closes with a brachah for the third Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: R' Mordechai Finkelman's words of thanks

summary.en: R' Mordechai Finkelman is called up and speaks about the seudas hodaah for the Mashgiach's recovery, which each participant feels is his own, and tells how the Mashgiach once advised him as a young man to return to camp rather than start a career.

title.en: R' Finkelman on mesiras nefesh in Shema

summary.en: R' Finkelman repeats ideas he heard on the mesiras nefesh of Shema Yisrael, ending with the thought that living with mesiras nefesh is greater than dying for Hashem, and that a person should see himself as a korban.

title.en: R' Finkelman's application and wishes

summary.en: R' Finkelman applies the idea to the kehillah: fixed times for learning, davening together and caring for one another, and closes with wishes for the Mashgiach's health and for the geulah.

catalogTitle: חיזוק: נועם שירת דור הצפרדע

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why the frog's song in Perek Shirah is 'Baruch shem kevod malchuso', and that the lowly generation of the footsteps of Moshiach is a generation of frogs whose song is especially dear to Hashem.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the reversal between land and sea: species impure on land are pure in the sea, and the reverse. He then brings the opening of Perek Shirah, where the frog tells King David that its song is finer than his, and the dispute of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah over 'the frog' in the singular. Through the Bnei Yissaschar and the Avnei Nezer he links the plague to the Egyptians' attempt to mix good with evil. He explains that every species sings through a pure counterpart that acts as its shliach tzibbur, but the frog lives on land and in the sea and has none, so its song is 'Baruch shem', the hidden praise of Hashem's presence even in impure places, said quietly. Tumah begins with 'two', which resolves the Midrash. He then applies this to our generation, the heel of Moshiach: a generation of frogs, facing new trials, whose weak service with mesiras nefesh is precious to Hashem, strengthened by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the week of hod, and he closes with the three 'remember's.

en: Every species sings to Hashem through its pure counterpart, but the frog, which belongs to both land and sea, has none, so its song in Perek Shirah is 'Baruch shem kevod malchuso'.
'Baruch shem' is the lower unity: Hashem watches over and sustains even the lowliest and impure places, a praise that is not fitting to proclaim aloud and is therefore said quietly.
The Mashgiach says our generation is the heel of Moshiach, facing new kinds of yetzer hara that never existed before, so it cannot hold on without mesiras nefesh.
Our generation is a generation of frogs, and its weak service in a time of hidden face is more precious to Hashem than the service of earlier generations.
The power of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, connected to hod, strengthens even the lowest souls in every generation.
The Mashgiach closes with the Torah's 'remember's: remember Amalek, because there is a great yetzer hara, and remember Miriam, so as not to spoil the frog's song with lashon hara and machlokes.

candidateTopics: purity of land and sea creatures
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and hod

title.en: Impure on land, pure in the sea

summary.en: After opening words and the verse of the stragglers attacked by Amalek, the Mashgiach brings the Ba'al HaTurim and the Gemara that the sea-donkey is pure and the sea-ox impure, and asks why Hashem reversed land and sea. He notes Tosafos limits this to those two animals, while the Divrei Yoel holds it is a general rule.

title.en: The frog and King David; one frog or many

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the opening of Perek Shirah, where a frog tells King David not to be proud because its song is finer than his, and wonders at it, since the frog's voice is the least pleasant. He then brings the Midrash on 'the frog' in the singular: Rabbi Akiva says one frog swarmed into multitudes, and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah rebukes him and says one frog whistled and the rest came.

title.en: The frog plague from yesod; mixing good and evil

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Bnei Yissaschar that the plague of frogs came from yesod, since the plagues went from below upward, and connects it to Pharaoh's plan to kill the males and take the females. Adding the Avnei Nezer that a mixture of good and evil is worse for Jews than evil itself, he explains the Egyptians wanted to create such a mixture.

title.en: The pure counterpart as shliach tzibbur

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that song must come in holiness and purity, so Hashem made each species pure in one realm and impure in the other; the pure one sings as shliach tzibbur for its impure counterpart. The frog lives in both the sea and on land, so no pure counterpart can sing for it; it is itself a mixture of tamei and tahor, fitting punishment for the Egyptians' mixture.

title.en: Baruch shem said quietly: the lower unity

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Pesachim that Yaakov's sons said Shema and Yaakov answered 'Baruch shem', which is said quietly like a princess craving the scrapings of the pot. Citing the Tanya's Shaar HaYichud and other sefarim, he explains Shema as the higher unity and Baruch shem as the lower unity, Hashem's providence even over impure places, which is not honorable to say aloud. He contrasts the sitra achra, which acknowledges Hashem but is not batel, like Bilam, with Avraham, who nullified his will at the Akeidah.

title.en: Why the frog's song is Baruch shem

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why, in Perek Shirah, the frog alone says no verse but 'Baruch shem kevod malchuso'. Having no pure shliach tzibbur, it may not say a verse, yet no creature's song may be missing, so it sings the lower unity quietly. He supports this with a Midrash that when a Jew says Shema the mazikin whisper 'Baruch shem', so they too have a right to exist.

title.en: Tumah begins with 'two'

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Rambam's explanation of the order of Seder Taharos, where Ohalos and then Negaim deal with the gravest tumah, and notes that both begin with the word 'two'. Twoness is the opposite of oneness: Gehinom and machlokes were created on the second day, and the same appears in the laws of carrying on Shabbos and false oaths.

title.en: Resolving Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah

summary.en: Returning to the Midrash, the Mashgiach explains that Rabbi Akiva's single frog as the root of the plague cannot be, since impurity cannot stem from oneness, and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah points to Negaim and Ohalos, which begin with 'two'. Yet the frog is a mixture, so the plague had both one and many: one frog whistled and the others came. The whistle, shuruk, is the vowel of yesod.

title.en: The heel of Moshiach and its new trials

summary.en: The Mashgiach says tzaddikim before the war foresaw that we are at the heel of Moshiach: the generations are like a body from head to heel, and ours is the lowest. Alongside many who learn and daven, new kinds of yetzer hara, such as the electronic one, are trapping even the finest, because the yetzer hara knows its end is near. He brings the Arizal's words to Rabbi Chaim Vital about a lowly generation, and calls ours a generation of the frog.

title.en: The frogs' mesiras nefesh and our song

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that Chananyah, Mishael and Azaryah learned mesiras nefesh from the frogs that jumped into the ovens, and says that today the whole world is a burning furnace and one cannot hold on without mesiras nefesh. Like the princess who preferred the scrapings of the pot, Hashem prefers the service of today's generation; the frog of Perek Shirah is today's Jew telling David's generation that its song is finer. Even a davening full of foreign thoughts is precious, because it is service in a time of hidden face.

title.en: Hod, the heel, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares our generation to the heel, which stays dark even under the summer sun, and to hod, the lowest sefirah and the left leg, as in Pesach Eliyahu. Citing the Beis Aharon, he says Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai gives strength to the lowest souls. Purim belongs to hod and to the stragglers whom Amalek attacks, the tribe of Dan according to Targum Yonasan, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the gematria of hod.

title.en: The week of hod and 'Roni akarah'

summary.en: The Mashgiach lays out the seven weeks from Pesach to Shavuos and from Tisha B'Av to Rosh Hashanah, and says the fifth week of consolation is the week of hod, when the parshah of Amalek is read. The haftarah 'Roni akarah' with 'for more are the children of the desolate' is explained by a Midrash: the righteous in exile are precious to Hashem, and the phrase is the gematria of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. Remembering Amalek is a reminder that there is a great yetzer hara.

title.en: A great yetzer hara; remember Miriam

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of an elder who, days before his passing, would say only that a tzaddik had said there is a great yetzer hara. He then brings the remembrance of Miriam: one should not spoil the frog's song with lashon hara and machlokes, and the three 'remember's of Shabbos, Amalek and Miriam are three trials to beware of. He closes with a brachah for teshuvah and the redemption.

catalogTitle: חנוכת הבית ל'שטיבל' בביתר: מסירת נפש לתפילה וענין דיבוק חבירים (מספר שומר אמונים)

oneLiner.en: At the opening of a new beis medrash, the Mashgiach teaches that in the days before Moshiach tefillah is the main avodah and demands constant mesiras nefesh, and that the foundation of the Ba'al Shem Tov's path is love between friends and among all Jews, as the sefer Shomer Emunim writes.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with thanks to those who built the new beis medrash and with the bracha 'matziv gevul almanah', explaining that Klal Yisroel is only 'like' a widow, since the Husband will return. Every new good thing draws the opposition of Amalek, and in the days before Moshiach nothing is achieved without mesiras nefesh. Tefillah, which Chazal call a thing standing at the height of the world yet treated lightly, is now the main avodah that will bring the geulah, so Amalek fights it most; one must ignore the scoffers and give up time and wishes daily, since many small sacrifices add up to more than one great one. He then explains the chassidic innovation of dibuk chaverim, citing the Divrei Chaim and the Ba'al Shem Tov, and reads at length from the Shomer Emunim on love of tzaddikim, friends and all Jews and on avoiding division. He explains that each shevet and each kehillah has its own nusach and ways from its own root above, that friends brought together share a root of the soul, and closes with brachos for the new beis medrash.

en: Every new good undertaking is attacked by Amalek, and in the days before Moshiach nothing can be achieved without mesiras nefesh.
In the days before Moshiach tefillah is the main avodah that will bring the geulah, though Torah study loses none of its greatness.
Constant mesiras nefesh is the great avodah: giving up any wish, such as a daily half hour to forty minutes for davening, is mesiras nefesh, and the small ones add up.
The Ba'al Shem Tov laid a great foundation on dibuk chaverim, and the Divrei Chaim explains that chassidic batei knesses are built on condition so that friends can eat and farbreng there.
Following the Shomer Emunim, love of tzaddikim, of friends and of all Jews is the heart of chassidus, and division between chassidic groups goes against the Ba'al Shem Tov's intent.
Each shevet has its own gate above and its own nusach and halachic ways, and people whom Providence brings together as friends share one root of the soul.

candidateTopics: tefillah in the days before Moshiach

title.en: Thanks and the bracha of the widow

summary.en: The Mashgiach thanks those who worked with great dedication to build the beis medrash and brings the bracha 'matziv gevul almanah' said over a rebuilt beis haknesses. He explains that Klal Yisroel is only 'like' a widow, for the Husband will return.

title.en: Amalek attacks every new beginning

summary.en: The Mashgiach says every good thing comes together with its opposite, and Amalek especially attacks the start of something new, so young men who begin a new undertaking must strengthen themselves against it. He cites a saying in the name of the Imrei Emes and of Belz that in the days before Moshiach nothing is reached without mesiras nefesh, and says the beis medrash is not built for a party but for avodas Hashem.

title.en: Tefillah as the main avodah before Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that tefillah stands at the height of the world yet people treat it lightly, and says that before Moshiach tefillah is the main avodah, illustrated by a sick man for whom orange juice matters more than bread. Amalek therefore fights tefillah most; one must ignore the scoffers and have constant mesiras nefesh, such as giving a half hour to forty minutes a day to davening.

title.en: Dibuk chaverim in the chassidic shtibel

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a 'bayis gadol' is one where Torah and tefillah are made great, and that chassidus brought a new element to the beis haknesses: dibuk chaverim. He cites the Divrei Chaim that chassidic shuls are built on condition so friends can eat and farbreng there, the Ba'al Shem Tov's foundation of love between friends and the Arizal's practice before davening, and says that today, amid great breaches, the shtibel must be a place where friends give each other advice in Yiddishkeit.

title.en: Shomer Emunim on love of friends and all Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads from the sefer Shomer Emunim that what remains from the tzaddikim of old is love of tzaddikim, of friends and of all Jews, that Klal Yisroel as a whole has no blemish, and that division between chassidic groups is against the Ba'al Shem Tov's will. He then applies it: going to a friend's simcha, helping families when a wife gives birth, and dealing with a wrongdoer gently rather than with zealotry that comes from one's own anger.

title.en: Against division and lashon hara between groups

summary.en: The Mashgiach continues reading the Shomer Emunim: through love of Jews one reaches the highest levels, the aim of the Ba'al Shem Tov's path is unity among Jews, and one must not speak lashon hara about any group of chassidim but seek mercy for others. Division, the sefer says, is complete falsehood, and the Mashgiach calls these great foundations.

title.en: Each shevet with its own gate and nusach

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls ahavas chaverim the foundation of the Ba'al Shem Tov's path, then explains the passuk of appointing judges 'for your tribes': each of the twelve shevatim has its own gate in heaven and its own nusach and halachic ways, as Sefardim and Ashkenazim differ today. He tells of Rav Chaim Ozer advising a man to move to Eretz Yisroel because of such a difference, and concludes that each kehillah has its own ways from its root at Matan Torah.

title.en: One root of the soul; brachos for the beis medrash

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that when Providence makes people friends it is a sign they share a root of the soul, and between them love must be stronger, as he cites from the Arizal. He closes with brachos that the beis medrash be a 'bayis gadol' for Torah, tefillah and love of friends and of all Jews, and with the hope of the rebuilt Beis Hamikdash.

catalogTitle: מעשה ברבי אליעזר וכו - What our Sages Accomplished in בני ברק

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the descendants of Haman who learned Torah in Bnei Brak carried a hidden holy point from Timna, and that the Tannaim came to Bnei Brak on Pesach to lift them to the level of Krias Shema.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a sefer's words that on Pesach a Jew can leave his straits not step by step. He then asks how descendants of Haman could learn Torah in Bnei Brak, when Hashem swore no converts would come from Amalek. His answer runs through Timna: she longed to cling to Avraham's family, and as a mere pilegesh to Eliphaz her holy point never merged with Amalek. Bringing the Kedushas Levi, he explains that Esther's seudah, prepared from Pesach food, drew Haman briefly out of tumah, and suggests that Zeresh, who escaped, carried that spark to the forebears of Rav Shmuel bar Shilas. Haman's descendants could not say Krias Shema of Shacharis, because of Zeresh's advice to hang Mordechai at daybreak. The Tannaim therefore came to Bnei Brak on Pesach and lifted Timna's children to Shema Yisrael. He closes with the father's descent to his children on Seder night.

en: The Mashgiach quotes a sefer that on Pesach a Jew can leave his straits all at once, not step by step as at other times.
Timna's longing to join Avraham's family was never lost; because she was only a pilegesh, her point stayed separate from Esav's and Amalek's seed.
That separate holy point is what allowed descendants of Haman to convert and learn Torah in Bnei Brak, among them Rav Shmuel bar Shilas.
Esther's seudah, made from Pesach food, brought Haman to the border of kedusha and roused in him the point from which Rav Shmuel bar Shilas would come.
Haman's descendants could not say Krias Shema of Shacharis, a trait from Zeresh's advice to hang Mordechai at daybreak; the Tannaim came to Bnei Brak on Pesach to lift them out of it.
On Seder night a father must go down from his highest levels and tell his young children the story of Yetzias Mitzrayim.

candidateTopics: Pesach as a time of leaving straits not step by step
descendants of Haman who learned Torah in Bnei Brak
Maaseh b'Rabbi Eliezer in Bnei Brak
telling children Yetzias Mitzrayim on Seder night

title.en: Timna and the descendants of Haman in Bnei Brak

summary.en: After opening with a sefer's words that on Pesach one can leave his straits all at once, the Mashgiach brings the Gemara about Menashe mocking the passuk of Timna and the Gemara that Haman's descendants learned Torah in Bnei Brak. He asks how this fits with the Midrash that no converts are accepted from Amalek.

title.en: Timna's longing and the pilegesh who stays apart

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a real longing shows a connection and is never lost, and that the first point of a thing endures even when hidden. Since Timna was only a pilegesh, who keeps her own identity unlike a wife, her point of longing for Avraham's seed stayed separate from Esav's seed and came out in Haman's descendants in Bnei Brak.

title.en: Haman's simcha and the escape of Zeresh

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Kedushas Levi's question how Haman could leave Esther's seudah happy when simcha exists only in kedusha: the seudah drew him out of tumah to the border of kedusha, leaving him no source of life. Comparing this to Agag, he suggests that Zeresh, who escaped, carried from that night the spark of Timna that later surfaced in Haman's descendants in Bnei Brak.

title.en: Ad d'lo yada: giving life to the holy spark

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ari HaKadosh's explanation of drinking until one does not know between cursed Haman and blessed Mordechai: a blessing on Haman said in drunkenness gives life to the holy point in him without feeding his klipah. He adds that a Jew who blesses Zeresh, perhaps Shilas the mother of Rav Shmuel, helps bring forth such a child.

title.en: Esther's Pesach seudah and Rav Shmuel bar Shilas

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Rav Shmuel bar Shilas is the source of the teaching that when Adar enters one increases simcha. Esther's seudah was made from the Pesach food she had prepared and not eaten during the fast, and Achashverosh loved such food; that kedusha gave Haman his simcha and roused the point of Rav Shmuel bar Shilas, so that his descendant taught the law of simcha.

title.en: Why Haman's descendants could not say Krias Shema

summary.en: The Mashgiach suggests that Haman's descendants in Bnei Brak could not say Krias Shema of Shacharis, comparing it to people who tell him they cannot say Krias Shema from overconcentration. He traces it to the Midrash on Zeresh's advice to hang Mordechai at daybreak, to stop his Krias Shema, and repeats that on Pesach a Jew can leap out of tumah.

title.en: The Tannaim come to Bnei Brak on Pesach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Tannaim chose Pesach to come to Bnei Brak and tell of Yetzias Mitzrayim, intending to benefit the souls of Haman's descendants and break Zeresh's klipah. He brings a sefer that mentioning Yetzias Mitzrayim relieves distress, and the Rambam in Perek Chelek that Shema Yisrael and 'va'achos Lotan Timna' are equally Torah.

title.en: From Timna to Shema; going down to the children

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that the Tannaim lifted the children of Timna, the 'lowest' passuk, to the level of saying Krias Shema, with the power of Pesach. He describes the holiness of Seder night and says that the Torah asks a great man to go down from his heights to tell his small children of Yetzias Mitzrayim, joining 'va'achos Lotan Timna' to Shema Yisrael.

catalogTitle: דרשה לנשים: חשיבות מסירת נפש בזמננו

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that in a time of crisis before the redemption, Hashem withholds the means for mitzvos like hachnasas kallah so that they are done with mesiras nefesh, the one weapon the Satan cannot stop, which will bring Moshiach.

abstract.en: Speaking at a gathering for hachnasas kallah, the Mashgiach opens with the pattern that the hardest stretch of exile comes just before the redemption: in Egypt, and in the time of Mordechai and Esther, when Haman's decree came seventy days before the miracle. He compares this to the present: Iran, the ancient Paras, threatens the Jews like a second Haman, and the economic crisis leaves people in despair and unable to help the many who ask. Why, he asks, does Hashem not give the money for the mitzvos He wants? Through the story of Yehuda and Tamar he shows that the Satan fights every opening for Moshiach, and that mesiras nefesh is the one weapon against him. Lot was saved by guests he took in with mesiras nefesh. Mesiras nefesh means acting against one's own will for Hashem, and now is the time for mitzvos done that way.

en: The hardest part of an exile comes right before the redemption, as in Egypt and in the days of Purim.
Hashem runs the world with hashgacha pratis, and the lack of money for tzedakah and hachnasas kallah is His doing, like Pharaoh's decree of bricks without straw.
The Satan works hardest to stop Moshiach, and the one weapon he cannot defeat is mesiras nefesh.
Yehuda's immediate admission to Tamar and Lot's hospitality were acts of mesiras nefesh that saved the line of Moshiach and saved Lot.
Mesiras nefesh does not only mean being killed; it means acting against one's own will for Hashem, and in these times mitzvos must be done that way.

candidateTopics: the Satan and the coming of Moshiach

title.en: The darkest hour before the redemption

summary.en: Opening at a gathering for hachnasas kallah, the Mashgiach describes how Pharaoh made the labor unbearable just before the Exodus, and how Haman's decree came seventy days before the Purim miracle. These, he says, were history-making days.

title.en: Iran, the economy, and a hard question

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares the present to Purim: Iran, once Paras, threatens the Jews like a second Haman, and he hopes for a repeat of the miracle there. He describes the despair over parnassa and the constant appeals, and asks why Hashem, who wants us to give and to marry off our children, does not give the money for it.

title.en: Yehuda's admission: mesiras nefesh in a moment

summary.en: The Mashgiach retells the episode of Yehuda and Tamar and explains that Yehuda's admission, 'she is more righteous than I', was great mesiras nefesh, made instantly because the fire had already been lit. He then asks why Tamar did not simply reveal openly that she was carrying Yehuda's children.

title.en: The one weapon against the Satan

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that the Satan, who will be destroyed when Moshiach comes, caused Er and Onan to sin; the only weapon against him is mesiras nefesh, so Tamar arranged that both she and Yehuda would have it. He adds that Lot was saved from Sodom because Hashem sent him guests, whom he took in with mesiras nefesh.

title.en: Hashem's present: tzedakah with mesiras nefesh

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Moshiach must come now, but the Satan holds him back, so Hashem sends a present as He did to Lot: needy people and fathers of kallahs, while the givers have only a little, so that giving takes mesiras nefesh. He tells of a tzaddik in Yerushalayim who collected for the poor again and again, and explained that the doctor prescribed a spoonful every hour.

title.en: What mesiras nefesh means today

summary.en: The Mashgiach defines mesiras nefesh as going against one's own will for Hashem, from the word nefesh in parshas Chayei Sarah, with examples from buying clothing and from helping kallahs. He brings the Gemara that the one who reviews the 101st time is the true oved Hashem, and closes with a brachah for the final redemption.

catalogTitle: סעודת ר”ח ניסן לאברכי אמ”י: DIGITAL ELECTRONICS הנסיון המיוחד שלנו

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that before Moshiach the Jewish people pass through a series of refining tests, that electronics are the test of today's generation, and that Nissan and Pesach give every Jew the power to renew himself and walk out of it.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Nissan as a time of renewal: Adam was created in Nissan, and each day of the dedication of the Nesi'im was a renewal, which the Ba'al Shem Tov tied to the thirteenth gate that includes all the tribes. He then brings Daniel's prophecy that before the end many will be sifted, whitened and refined like silver. These refinings, he says, began about three hundred years ago: Shabbetai Tzvi, the Frankists, Reform in Germany, the emptiness of early America, Communism and Zionism, each of which tore away multitudes. Today's test is electronics, an addiction like alcoholism whose core desire is immorality and which removes the taste of davening, learning and the Seder. Yet every Jew can leave Mitzrayim and become a new person in Nissan, when all of nature is renewed. The Mashgiach calls for a firm 'no', throwing out the devices with the chametz, and binding oneself to Hashem through Pesach.

en: Nissan is a time when a Jew must renew himself like a newborn child, because Adam was actually created in Nissan.
Before Moshiach the Jewish people go through refinings, as Daniel says that many will be sifted, whitened and refined like silver in a furnace.
The refinings began about three hundred years ago with Shabbetai Tzvi and continued through the Frankists, Reform, Communism and Zionism, each of which tore away multitudes of Jews.
The test of today's generation is electronics, an addiction like alcoholism that takes away the taste of davening, learning and the Seder; it is probably the last test before Moshiach.
Even one caught in it can get out, because every Jew can leave Mitzrayim and become a new person in Nissan.
The Mashgiach calls for a strong 'no' to the yetzer hara: throwing out the devices together with the chametz, since chametz and matzah cannot exist together.
Pesach, unlike Shavuos and Sukkos, carries kares, because it is the point of emunah and of tearing oneself free, and whoever keeps it binds himself to Hashem.

candidateTopics: electronics and technology as a spiritual test
Nissan as a time of renewal

title.en: Nissan, the Nesi'im and the thirteenth gate

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Nissan as a month of renewal, when Adam was created and a Jew should become like a newborn. He describes each day of the dedication of the Nesi'im as a renewal and explains why the Ba'al Shem Tov's followers did not say the siddur's prayer about one's own tribe: today every Jew belongs to the thirteenth gate that includes all the tribes.

title.en: Daniel's prophecy of the refinings

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Pesach bright days to be used, citing his rebbe, Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz. He then explains that before Moshiach there will be tests to determine who merits the redemption, bringing the end of Daniel that many will be sifted, whitened and refined like silver in a furnace.

title.en: Three hundred years of refining

summary.en: The Mashgiach traces the refinings of the last three hundred years: Shabbetai Tzvi, the Frankists, and Reform, which destroyed German Jewry as the Meshech Chochmah foresaw. He connects this to the 'book' in Daniel and Malachi in which those who stay loyal are written, and describes the early immigrants in America who lost their children.

title.en: Communism and Zionism

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Communism, which emptied the great chassidic centers of Russia within seventy years and was the first kingdom of heresy, as the Gemara at the end of Sotah foretells. He then describes Zionism, which taught that a land and a language make a Jew; both movements have collapsed, but the destruction they left remains.

title.en: Electronics, today's test

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls electronics the test of today's generation. From what people tell him as mashgiach, he describes it as an addiction like alcoholism, whose core desire is immorality, which takes away the taste of davening, Gemara and the Seder. He says it is probably the last test before Moshiach and that knowing this can help one save others.

title.en: Every Jew can leave Mitzrayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that one sunk in these desires cannot praise Hashem with kedushah, and brings the end of the parsha of tzitzis: 'you shall be holy', 'I am Hashem who took you out of Mitzrayim'. Every Jew can leave Mitzrayim and must show himself as having left it. Today's test also includes hester panim, so it all rests on emunah and on holding onto the mitzvos of Pesach.

title.en: A new people, a renewed nature

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that at the Exodus the Jews became a new people and that every Jew becomes a Jew through it, citing the Maharal. This renewal comes down into nature: the blessing over the blossoming trees, the haftarah of the dry bones on Pesach, and the spring described in Shir HaShirim. When all of nature is renewed, a Jew should not be the exception.

title.en: The drunkard, and throwing out the chametz

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a drunkard who held back for three days and then rewarded himself with a drink, and draws from it the need for one strong 'no'. He calls to throw out the devices together with the chametz, the true spiritual chametz, since chametz and matzah cannot coexist, and describes Pesach as the time when everything becomes new.

title.en: Why Pesach carries kares

summary.en: Citing the Chiddushei HaRim, the Mashgiach explains that although Shavuos and Sukkos are higher, only Pesach carries kares, like milah, because it is the point of emunah and of Avraham Avinu; whoever keeps it becomes bound to Hashem. He closes with the hope that the treasured people bind themselves to Hashem, and with l'chaim and wishes for a kosher and happy Pesach.

catalogTitle: אסון בברא פארק: דברי חיזוק אחר האסון בבארא פארק

oneLiner.en: After the tragedy in Boro Park, the Mashgiach shows from Pinchas's zealotry, done as one of Klal Yisrael, how the Jewish people revealed their true holiness this week, and strengthens them with emunah in hashgachah pratis and the comfort of Parshas Pinchas.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Pinchas, who received the kehunah only through his zealotry, and asks what the Torah means by saying he was zealous 'in their midst'. He explains that Pinchas did not act as someone above Klal Yisrael but as a simple member of it, showing that the Jewish people are holy and separate from Zimri, whom he describes as a Jew with a foreign growth attached to him. This week, he says, a Jew became such a Zimri, while thousands of Jews in Boro Park searched all night and the levayah was a great kiddush Hashem, showing the signs of the Jewish people: merciful, bashful and doers of kindness. He then explains that Parshas Pinchas is a comfort, with Eliyahu and the festivals, and that this rare year it falls outside the Three Weeks by hashgachah. He reads from Tzafun Lashomer Emunim on believing that everything is guided by Hashem, and closes by calling to receive Shabbos with joy.

en: Pinchas was zealous 'in their midst': not as someone above Klal Yisrael but as a simple member of it, to show that the Jewish people are holy.
Zimri was a Jew to whom a foreign growth had attached itself, and this week a Jew became such a Zimri.
The thousands who searched all night and the levayah revealed the signs of the Jewish people: merciful, bashful and doers of kindness.
Parshas Pinchas is a comfort, and this year it falls outside the Three Weeks by hashgachah, so that Jews have comfort after this week's tragedy.
Everything that happens is guided by Hashem; when Moshiach comes it will be understood, and now one must believe that it was all for good.

candidateTopics: signs of the Jewish people: mercy, bashfulness, kindness

title.en: Pinchas's zealotry 'in their midst'

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Pinchas received the kehunah only through his zealotry, knowing he might lose it, and asks what 'in their midst' means. He answers that Pinchas acted not as someone higher than Klal Yisrael but as a simple Jew among them, to show that the Jewish people are holy.

title.en: A Zimri this week, and Klal Yisrael's response

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Zimri as a Jew to whom a foreign growth attached itself, and says that this week a Jew became such a Zimri. Against this, thousands of Jews from Boro Park and elsewhere searched all night, the levayah was a great kiddush Hashem, and the Jewish people showed they are merciful, bashful and doers of kindness.

title.en: Parshas Pinchas as comfort, by hashgachah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parshas Pinchas, with Eliyahu, the korbanos and the festivals, is a comfort in the Three Weeks, and that this rare year it falls outside them, with the haftarah of Eliyahu. Nothing is by chance; the tragedy is part of the tikkun of souls that will be understood when Moshiach comes, and now one must believe it was for good.

title.en: Emunah in hashgachah, and comfort through Shabbos

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads from the Tzafun Lashomer Emunim a text on the principles of faith: that Hashem is good and merciful and everything, even the suffering of tzaddikim, is guided by Him. He returns to the beauty of Klal Yisrael shown this week, and closes that one must be strengthened and comforted by Shabbos and receive it with joy.

catalogTitle: The Seven Middos of Sefirah; The קדושה of כלל ישראל vs. the טומאה of ישמעאל

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains the seven middos that are refined during the seven weeks of Sefirah, and shows that Yishmael is the klipah of Yesod, which is why the present galus brings such hard tests of kedushah and why guarding that kedushah decides the struggle over Eretz Yisroel.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach sets out to explain, in simple pshat, what the seven weeks of Sefirah are about. Hashem's attributes come down into this world in reduced form, like steam becoming water and ice, and appear as seven middos in every person, each usable for good or bad. He goes through chesed, gevurah, tiferes, netzach, hod, yesod and malchus, with their Avos, limbs and examples, and explains that each week one middah is to be purified. He then sets the seven Ushpizim against seven forces of tumah and turns to Yishmael: the Rambam's Iggeres Teiman calls them haters of peace, and the Zohar explains that their empty milah gave them Eretz Yisroel only while it was empty. Yishmael is the klipah of yesod, the one who sold Yosef to Mitzrayim, the ervas ha'aretz. The present summer's tests of tznius are part of a heavenly din Torah over Eretz Yisroel, decided in the yeshivos by Torah, tefillah and guarding the eyes.

en: The seven middos in a person are reduced forms of Hashem's attributes, the same substance in a more physical form, like steam, water and ice.
Each middah can be used for avodas Hashem or for the wrong things, and each of the seven weeks of Sefirah is given to purify one middah in preparation for Matan Torah.
Just as seven Ushpizim embody the seven middos in kedushah, seven nations embody them in tumah, and Yishmael is the klipah of yesod.
Yishmael held Eretz Yisroel through the galus only because his empty milah earned him the land while it stood empty; now that Jews are returning, that claim is being contested.
The present era is the time of the klipah of yesod, which is why the tests of tznius grow harder every summer.
The heavenly din Torah over Eretz Yisroel is decided in the yeshivos and batei medrash, through Torah, tefillah and guarding the eyes and thoughts.

title.en: Seven middos, from heaven to man

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens by saying many count Sefirah without knowing what the words mean, and promises a simple pshat. He explains that Hashem's attributes come down reduced, with the mashal of steam, water and ice, and that of the ten maamaros seven came down into this world and into a person's character.

title.en: No reshus: every act is mitzvah or aveirah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a person can use his seven middos for avodas Hashem or for aveiros, since there is no neutral reshus. Eating for health to serve Hashem is a mitzvah, while indulging even in kosher food is what the Ramban on this week's sedrah condemns; the seven weeks are given to sanctify one middah each week.

title.en: Chesed, gevurah and tiferes

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains chesed as ahavah, linked to Avraham and Pesach's Shir HaShirim; gevurah as yirah and pachad Yitzchak, with the example of a dayan wrongly afraid of a powerful litigant; and tiferes as harmony and pride, shown by a sunset and music, which belongs only with Hashem.

title.en: Netzach, hod, yesod and malchus

summary.en: The Mashgiach matches the middos to the limbs and explains netzach as fighting to win and hod as yielding, the two legs on which a person stands; yesod as the drive for continuity, tied to bris milah; and malchus as bitul to Hashem, the middah of Shabbos and David HaMelech. He then says that the week of netzach starting that night means rising against the yetzer hara.

title.en: Gevurah within chesed, and Kedoshim tihyu

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that each middah has subdivisions, illustrating gevurah shebechesed with a mother who holds her baby tightly on the stairs out of love. He explains the request after counting that the flaw in that day's middah be repaired, and brings Rashi and the Ramban on Kedoshim tihyu.

title.en: Yishmael, the hater of peace

summary.en: The Mashgiach sets the seven Ushpizim against the seven nations of Canaan as the middos in tumah, then turns to the Rambam's Iggeres Teiman, which calls the galus of Yishmael harder than that of Edom. He explains from the passuk about the tents of Kedar that Yishmael hates peace, and applies it to the current conflict.

title.en: Yishmael's empty milah and Eretz Yisroel

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why only Yishmael has held Eretz Yisroel since the Churban, and brings the Zohar: Yishmael's angel claimed the land for keeping milah, and was told his milah is empty, so he would hold the land while it is empty. He explains that Yishmael's middah is yesod in tumah, bringing the Gemara that nine of ten measures of znus went to Yishmael.

title.en: Azazel and the Kohen Gadol's miracle

summary.en: From the Yom Kippur reading the Mashgiach explains that the sins are placed on Esav because a Jew's inner will is to do Hashem's will and the yetzer hara, Esav's angel, causes the sin, as shown by the Rambam on compelling a person until he says he wants. He then brings the Tosfos Yom Tov's answer why it was a miracle that the Kohen Gadol never became tamei on Yom Kippur: the Satan concentrated all his power on him.

title.en: Yishmael, Yosef and Mitzrayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains what a klipah is with the mashal of a peel, and that Yishmael, the klipah of yesod, pursues Yosef, the tzaddik of yesod: it was Yishmaelim who sold Yosef to Mitzrayim. Using the three dimensions of place, time and soul, he calls Mitzrayim the place of the klipah of yesod, the ervas ha'aretz, as against Tziyon.

title.en: The time of the klipah of yesod

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why each summer the tests of tznius grow harder, recalling how different the street was when he was a boy, and answers that the end of galus is galus Yishmael, the time of the klipah of yesod. He explains that the world's focus on Eretz Yisroel reflects a din Torah in Shamayim, fought not by armies but in the yeshivos through Torah, tefillah and guarding the eyes.

title.en: The geulah is in the bochur's hands

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that a Jew who turns his eyes away fights the war against Yishmael, and that the geulah depends not on Washington but on Torah, tefillah, tzedakah and guarding yesod. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar that all of Sefirah is about rectifying yesod, recalls how Yosef's kedushah saved the Jews in Mitzrayim, and ends with a wish that the bochurim pass the summer's test and bring Moshiach.

catalogTitle: הכרת הטוב: נודה לך ונספר

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that hod, thanks and self-effacement, is the root of a Jew, from Modeh Ani each morning to the Korban Pesach, and that this power belongs most of all to the lowest souls whom Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai lifts up.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the six hundred thousand letters of the Torah that match the six hundred thousand souls: the first letters are Moshe, David and Moshiach, the last ones the lowest souls of the generations before Moshiach. Souls are also ordered by the middos, and ours are of hod, the lowest; hod shebehod is Lag BaOmer, the day of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who sees the hidden worth of even the lowest Jew. Hod means beauty, thanks and submission. Leah thanked Hashem at Yehudah's birth for receiving more than her share, so kingship, which demands that the king stay small, went to Yehudah. A Jew's first word each day is Modeh Ani, and the Korban Pesach, the first offering, is a thanks offering of pure kindness. Modeh Ani is said with impure hands to declare that the kelipah is nothing, as Avraham did with dust. The Mashgiach ends with Pesach Sheini, the Alter Rebbe's day and thanks for the final redemption.

en: The souls of the last generations are souls of hod, the lowest level, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, whose day is hod shebehod, reveals the hidden worth in them.
Hod means beauty, thanks and submission; Leah's thanks at Yehudah's birth came from feeling she had received more than her share.
Kingship belongs to Yehudah because a king must hold himself no higher than the lowest Jew, and only one rooted in thanks can do so.
A Jew's first word each morning, Modeh Ani, sets the tone of the whole day, since everything follows its beginning.
The Korban Pesach, the first offering of the Jewish people, is a thanks offering for a redemption that came through Hashem's kindness and not through their deeds.
Modeh Ani is said even with impure hands to declare that the kelipah has no power before Hashem, and through this declaration it is nullified.

title.en: Opening

summary.en: The opening of the shiur.

title.en: Souls of hod and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai

summary.en: The Mashgiach matches the letters of the Torah to the souls, from Moshe, David and Moshiach at the start to the lowest souls at the end, and explains that our souls are of hod. Hod shebehod is Lag BaOmer, the day of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who sees and reveals the hidden worth of the lowest Jews.

title.en: Hod as thanks: Leah and Yehudah

summary.en: The Mashgiach lists the meanings of hod: beauty, thanks and submission. He brings Leah's words at Yehudah's birth and Rashi's explanation that she received more than her share, and explains that a Jew who knows everything is a gift bows in thanks, as at Modim.

title.en: Why kingship belongs to Yehudah; Modeh Ani

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a king must not hold himself above his brothers, which is why kingship was given to Yehudah, born of Leah's thanks, and he brings David who stayed small. Since everything follows its beginning, a Jew's first word, Modeh Ani, must leave its mark on the whole day; this is why a Jew is called Yehudi.

title.en: The Korban Pesach as a thanks offering

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Exodus came not by merit but because the Jews are Hashem's children, so the first offering, the Korban Pesach, is a thanks offering. He brings the Abarbanel's question why it has no chametz loaves, and answers that it is an offering of pure kindness, not of deeds.

title.en: Modeh Ani with impure hands

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Hayom Yom that Modeh Ani is said before washing, and asks why one does not wash first. He explains that declaring the world nothing before Hashem nullifies evil, as in bittul chametz and Avraham's dust against the kings, and brings the Gemara in Shabbos about the 'king's daughter' on the fingers who insists on proper washing.

title.en: The true prince and Pesach Sheini

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the proud 'king's daughter' of the kelipah with the Jew, a true king's son who makes himself small; his Modeh Ani with impure hands nullifies her. He then explains Pesach Sheini: the impure argued that the Korban Pesach, like Modeh Ani, could be brought in impurity, and it was instead set in the week of hod to show that even the lowest souls bring it.

title.en: The Alter Rebbe's day and closing thanks

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a teaching linking the twenty-fourth of Teves to Lag BaOmer, and explains that the Alter Rebbe and his successors continued Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's work of raising the lowest Jew through shluchim. He closes with thanks to Hashem, mentions birthdays being marked, his own among them, and wishes for the final redemption.

catalogTitle: המצב ב: התעוררי! התעוררי!

oneLiner.en: Faced with the Iranian threat to destroy the Jewish people, the Mashgiach calls on Jews to wake up from their indifference and answer the danger with teshuvah, tefillah, Torah, chessed and unity, trusting that Hashem's evident miracles point toward salvation.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Rambam in Hilchos Taaniyos: it is a mitzvah to cry out to Hashem in every communal trouble, and treating a trouble as mere chance is cruelty that brings further troubles. He then describes the present danger: the leader of Iran openly threatens to kill every Jew, like Haman, and seeks a nuclear bomb, yet people stay silent and busy with trivialities. Without panic, he reads the Pesikta Rabbasi on the kings of Persia and Arabia provoking each other before Moshiach's coming, noting how closely it resembles the present. He points to the miracles Hashem has shown in Eretz Yisrael, and learns from Manoach's wife that such wonders signal salvation, but, citing Rav Tzadok on Eliyahu, insists one must still pray. He calls for Torah, chessed and tefillah, undisturbed learning, special prayers, and above all unity, as in the days of Haman.

en: According to the Rambam, crying out to Hashem in a communal trouble is a mitzvah and part of the path of teshuvah, and calling the trouble mere chance is cruelty that brings more troubles.
The Mashgiach says the Iranian leader's open threat to kill every Jew is a terrible danger, and the general silence and indifference toward it is a great wrong.
The miracles Hashem has shown in Eretz Yisrael are, like the wonders Manoach and his wife saw, a sign that Hashem intends salvation and not harm.
Even with Hashem's assurance of salvation, one must still pray and do teshuvah, as Rav Tzadok learns from Eliyahu praying for the rain he had been promised.
To be saved from the birth pangs of Moshiach one must strengthen Torah and chessed, with fixed, intense learning that is not interrupted by the telephone.
Haman's decree was annulled through the gathering and unity of all the Jews, and the Mashgiach calls for the same love and unity now, approaching Shabbos Shekalim and Adar.

title.en: The Rambam: crying out in times of trouble

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the Rambam in Hilchos Taaniyos that it is a mitzvah to cry out and sound the trumpets in every communal trouble, as part of the path of teshuvah. He explains the Rambam's warning that calling a trouble mere chance is cruelty that only brings further troubles.

title.en: The Iranian threat and the silence

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the Iranian leader's declared intent to kill every Jew and his pursuit of a nuclear bomb, and asks why people stay silent and indifferent instead of crying out and praying. He tells of his request for a gathering and of Rav Rosenblum's words that this is a time of judgment for the whole community and every individual.

title.en: Persia and Arabia in the Pesikta

summary.en: The Mashgiach says there is no cause for panic and reads the Pesikta Rabbasi about the year of Moshiach's revelation, when the king of Persia provokes the king of Arabia and Hashem tells Yisrael that the time of redemption has come. With the Gemara on Edom and Paras and the Maharal linking Paras to Yishmael, he notes the striking resemblance to today, while saying no one can know for sure.

title.en: Miracles as a sign, yet prayer is needed

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the miracles in Eretz Yisrael, where missiles fall and almost no one is hurt, and learns from Manoach's wife that such wonders show Hashem intends salvation. Yet, citing Rav Tzadok on Eliyahu and a Midrash on the wall of water at the Yam Suf, he insists that even with a promise one must pray and do teshuvah.

title.en: Torah and chessed against chevlei Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Sanhedrin that Torah and gemilus chasadim save from the birth pangs of Moshiach, and the passuk in Tzefanyah, and calls for prayer, a cheshbon hanefesh and fixed, fiery learning. He explains that learning is like Shabbos, so the phone should not interrupt it and the beis medrash must not become a marketplace.

title.en: Unity against Haman, then and now

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Haman's decree was annulled through the unity of all the Jews, recommends specific prayers, including the kapitel Tehillim the Belzer Rav instituted against wars, and cites the Gemara to pray before trouble comes. Through the half shekel and Korach's dispute he teaches that unity is the remedy, and closes with a call to approach Shabbos Shekalim and Adar with joy and bitachon.

catalogTitle: סיום השס: סיום השס בבית מדרש אמונת ישראל בביתר

oneLiner.en: At a siyum haShas, the Mashgiach explains from the Ba'al HaTanya and the Midrash that every member of a group that finishes Shas together shares in the whole Shas and in its 'kingship', and asks that the merit of Torah learning bring the redemption.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach calls it a great privilege to join a group in Eretz Yisroel completing Shas. He brings the Ba'al HaTanya's request at the end of the Tanya that every town divide the masechtos each year and finish Shas, small minyanim joining a larger one. From this he learns that each member is connected to the whole Shas, as the Lubavitcher Rebbe explains, through the bond of souls among them. He brings the Midrash on 'sixty are the queens', the sixty masechtos, and explains that whoever learns a masechta, or even halachah after halachah, merits a share of 'malchus'. Turning to the present, he says the situation grows sharper and Jews need a great salvation; when Jews in Eretz Yisroel and abroad learn and daven for each other, their tefillos join through Yerushalayim. He mentions the Midrash that learning Mishnah among the nations brings the ingathering of exiles, and closes with a prayer for the great nechamah.

en: The Ba'al HaTanya asks that every town divide the masechtos each year and complete Shas, and that small minyanim join a larger one to do it.
In a group that finishes Shas, each member is connected to the whole Shas and is counted as having finished it, through the bond of souls among them.
Based on the Midrash on 'sixty are the queens', whoever learns a masechta, or even one halachah after another, gains a share in 'malchus'.
Jews today need a great salvation, and when Jews in Eretz Yisroel and abroad learn and daven for one another their tefillos are joined together through Yerushalayim.
The merit of Jews learning Torah everywhere should bring the ingathering of the exiles and the great nechamah.

title.en: Every member shares in the whole Shas

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ba'al HaTanya's call to divide and finish Shas in every town and learns from it that each member of the group is bound to the whole Shas. He then brings the Midrash on 'sixty are the queens' to show that learning a masechta, or even single halachos, gives a share in malchus.

title.en: Torah learning and tefillah for the redemption

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the situation grows sharper and Jews need a great salvation; tefillos of Jews in Eretz Yisroel and abroad join through Yerushalayim. He brings the Midrash that learning Mishnah among the nations brings the ingathering of exiles, and closes with a prayer for the great nechamah and wishes to begin Shas again.

catalogTitle: Why the תלמידי ר' עקיבא Stopped Dying When the Week of ל”ג בעומר Arrived

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Rabbi Akiva's talmidim died because they honored each other only for visible virtues, and that the dying stopped in the week of Hod when Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, revealer of the Torah's secrets, taught them that every Jew carries a hidden secret that makes him precious to Hashem.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a saying that whoever believes in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai can draw chizuk from him, since he is for every Jew. He asks how Rabbi Akiva's talmidim could have failed to respect each other. Just as the Torah has pshat, remez, drush and sod, every Jew has a hidden sod; citing the Chiddushei HaRim, he says every Jew finds unique favor with Hashem through a trait no one can identify. The talmidim respected only visible greatness, so the respect between chavrusos ran one way. The week of Hod, the middah of yielding, calls for honoring even a lesser chavrusa. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who revealed the Torah's secrets after the Churban, taught this on Lag BaOmer, his day, and the decree ended. Pesach Sheini, given to the temei'im in the week of Hod, and the link between Lag BaOmer and Purim show the same point, as does the Ohr HaChaim's teaching that the final day of redemption comes even for complete reshaim.

en: Just as the Torah has pshat, remez, drush and sod, every Jew has a hidden sod that no one else can see.
The sin of Rabbi Akiva's talmidim was that respect between chavrusos went only from the lesser to the greater, based on visible virtues.
Hod is the middah of yielding and subordination, and its tikkun is to respect even a chavrusa who is lesser in every visible way.
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who revealed the secrets of the Torah, taught the talmidim on Lag BaOmer that every Jew carries a sod, and then the decree ended.
Pesach Sheini, a special day given to the temei'im in the week of Hod, shows that every Jew has a sod for which he is worthy.
Lag BaOmer and Purim share one character: both show that Hashem finds favor even in the lowest Jew.
The final day of the Geulah, which comes even for complete reshaim, is itself a sod, because it comes through the sod in every Jew.

title.en: Chizuk from Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the question

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with a saying that whoever believes in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai can draw chizuk from him, as he is for every Jew, like Hashem. He raises the question of how Rabbi Akiva's talmidim could have failed to respect each other, and introduces pshat, remez, drush and sod, with sod revealed by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, paralleled by the four levels of the soul.

title.en: Every Jew is a letter in the Sefer Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the 600,000 souls correspond to the letters of the Torah: each is unique, and a missing letter invalidates the Sefer Torah. He brings the Chiddushei HaRim that every Jew finds special favor with Hashem through a trait of his own, and that no one can know in this world which trait it is.

title.en: The hidden sod and the one-way respect

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Jew has pshat, remez, drush and a hidden sod known only to Hashem. Rabbi Akiva's talmidim judged each other by visible virtues: among the 12,000 pairs of chavrusos, the lesser respected the greater but not the reverse, and that was their flaw.

title.en: The week of Hod: the middah of yielding

summary.en: The Mashgiach goes through the seven middos of the weeks of Sefirah and explains Netzach and Hod as the two legs that support the body: victory and yielding. Hod is surrender, as in the reed that bends before the wind, and its tikkun is to respect even a lesser chavrusa because he has something one lacks.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai reveals the secrets

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks who made the talmidim aware of the hidden sod in every Jew, and answers: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, then a youngster among them. Like Yechezkel, who saw the Merkavah after the first Churban to encourage the Jews in galus, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai revealed the Zohar after the second Churban.

title.en: Lag BaOmer: his day, and the decree ends

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every person has a day when his mazal is strongest, and Lag BaOmer is Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's day. On that day he succeeded in teaching the talmidim to respect even a lesser chavrusa because of the sod he carries, the talmidim began respecting each other and the decree ended, and so it is a double simcha.

title.en: Pesach Sheini: a day for the temei'im

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks what the temei'im who said 'lamah nigara' were arguing, since their impurity obviously excluded them, and why Moshe did not answer them directly. He explains that Pesach celebrates becoming Jews, so Hashem agreed and gave them the first day of Hod; why that date was chosen has no answer, since it is a sod, like the hidden worth of every Jew.

title.en: Lag BaOmer and Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach connects Lag BaOmer to Purim, the Yom Tov for the low and the stragglers whom Amalek attacked. He brings the Shulchan Aruch's at-bash rule, in which 'peleg' teaches that Lag BaOmer falls on the same weekday as Purim, and concludes that Hashem even made a special Yom Tov, Pesach Sheini, for the impure.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon for every Jew, and the sod of the Geulah

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to the opening saying: emunah in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is emunah in the sod of the Torah, which tells even the simplest Jew that he is precious to Hashem. He brings the Ohr HaChaim, similar to the Ramban, that the final day of the Geulah comes even for complete reshaim because of the sod in every Jew, and closes that there are secrets in the Torah, in every Jew and in the Geulah.

catalogTitle: חיזוק: גודל אהבת ה' אלינו

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem's love for Klal Yisrael has levels that can never be cut off, so that even after the breaking of the luchos brought forgetting, Hashem does not forget Sinai and cannot exchange the Jewish people.

abstract.en: After brief introductions, the Mashgiach ties Elul's 'Ani l'dodi' to the seven haftaros of consolation: after six weeks of silence, Klal Yisrael answers on the seventh with 'Sos asis' as a bride. He turns to 'Vatomer Tziyon azavani Hashem' and the Gemara in Berachos: the golden calf will be forgotten, but Hashem will not forget Sinai. Since the breaking of the luchos brought forgetting into the world, he asks how one can be forgotten and not the other. Bringing the Maharal on the luchos as the bond between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, and the Midrash in which the king calls his daughter 'my daughter', 'my sister' and 'my mother', he explains that higher levels of love act as a backup that cannot be severed. A Gemara about an esrog of terumah and Rashi in Nitzavim show that Jews are Hashem's terumah and cannot be exchanged. He closes with Yom Kippur, Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah, and the purpose of the yeshiva.

en: In the seventh week of consolation Klal Yisrael finally accepts the consolation and answers Hashem as a bride, with 'Sos asis'.
The Gemara in Berachos teaches that the golden calf will be forgotten but Hashem will not forget Sinai, which seems to contradict itself: either there is forgetting or there is not.
The breaking of the luchos brought forgetting into the world, and threatened to make even the bond between Hashem and Klal Yisrael forgotten.
Hashem's love for Klal Yisrael has three levels, like a king who calls his daughter 'my daughter', 'my sister' and 'my mother', and the higher levels serve as a backup that cannot be severed.
Klal Yisrael is Hashem's terumah, 'the first of His crop', and just as terumah has no redemption, Hashem cannot exchange the Jewish people for another nation.
Simchas Torah ends the Torah with 'l'einei kol Yisrael', the breaking of the luchos, and at once begins Bereishis, to show that Klal Yisrael is not forgotten.
